doc.title: Greg Thomas interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 2014

title: Coaching young musicians to entertain
summary: Thomas tells young musicians to communicate with audiences, and Rowe suggests jazz schools do not teach this.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah. Absolutely. You know one of the things that, particularly when we’ve hired young musicians I realized that I’m going to have to not only just hire and produce an event featuring young musicians, but sometimes I actually need to get into a coaching modality with them in the sense of, “Hey guys, this is entertainment too. This is entertainment. So you need to communicate with your audience. You know, maybe you’re interacting. You tell some jokes or you let them know what song it is, and you give them a context to connect with you and to connect with the music. It’s got to be more than you just getting up there blowing.”

Yeah. Listen to Cannonball Adderley and how he — and it’s really interesting you say that because I’m guessing that some of these younger musicians that don’t get that may have graduated from jazz schools.
I think so. I think so, yeah.
